doc.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998

title: Piano Jazz, Billy Taylor and discouragement
summary: Brief mention of Marian McPartland and Billy Taylor; she recalls when she felt like quitting.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I guess. I understood you did “Piano Jazz” with Marian McPartland?
Sure. And I interviewed with Billy Taylor. I mean I’ve been through it. You know, been through it. Ups and downs you know.
Did you ever have a point where you felt like, man this is just too hard. I can’t do this anymore.

Sure you say that to yourself sometimes. One of the times when I was feeling like that was when I wrote that letter to NASA. And look what happened. Somehow you pull yourself up, somehow. And the music pulls you up you know. Anytime you just play, that’s the kind of magic that makes you want it more, and you keep striving for that moment again. That’s what we live for. It’s in the music I think that gets you through all that hard stuff.
